text:
Noam Chomsky is a prominent political dissident and linguist, renowned for co-founding analytic philosophy. In linguistics, he is credited with inaugurating the "cognitive revolution," establishing the field as a formal, natural science, and is known for developing transformational grammar. He critically challenged the behaviorist paradigm of B. F. Skinner, arguing that language is a unique evolutionary development of the human species rooted in innate, biologically preset principles, a view formalized in his theory of universal grammar.
Beyond linguistics, Chomsky is a major figure in sociopolitical analysis. He is a prominent critic of American imperialism and has written extensively on international affairs, particularly focusing on U.S. foreign policy. He advocates for a "scientific society" where war is abolished and population growth is limited, and he supports guild socialism and libertarian socialism. His political activism includes being a prominent campaigner against the Vietnam War and nuclear disarmament. He has faced criticism regarding his views on certain geopolitical issues and his defense of free speech principles, even when applied to controversial figures.
